Technical review (one risk + one typed refactor per excerpt):

1) `zig/src/server/slide_correction_source.zig` — defines `pub fn independent(srv: *Server, cx: *errors.Cx, h: teach.Held, old: []const u8, ids: []const u32, gone: anytype) !void`.
- Risk: `names` is an `std.ArrayList(u8)` built with `.empty` and never deinit'd (leak), and the match check `correction.oldReturned(h.question, old, old, f.text)` passes `old` twice, so the "kept value matches the old answer" test is degenerate and can miss a real match. `gone: anytype` also erases the type of the reads dependency.
- Refactor: introduce a typed `RefusalNames` builder (with `deinit(cx.a)`) and a concrete `GoneFacts`/`Reads` interface instead of `anytype`; pass `old` once and the fact text once.

2) `zig/src/metal/sync.zig` — defines `SharedEvent` (`value`, `set`, `wait`, `deinit`) and `Event` (`deinit`).
- Risk: `SharedEvent.deinit` releases `id` but leaves the struct value usable; a second `deinit` or a `value()`/`wait()` after release double-releases/uses a dangling `Id`. `wait` also collapses timeout into a bare `bool` with no error path.
- Refactor: make `SharedEvent` a consuming handle — `deinit(self: *SharedEvent)` sets `id = 0` (or takes ownership), and `wait` returns `!bool`/`!void` with a typed timeout error.

3) `zig/src/families/hy4_flash/index_cuda.zig` — defines `Weights`, `Indexer` (`load`, `deinit`, `cacheKeys`, `poolGroups`, `select`), `Keys`, `Select`, and `closedBy`.
- Risk: `cacheKeys` validates `b.count` against `b.gemm_rows` but never checks `b.first_slot + b.count` against the cache capacity, so `cache.copyFrom(b.first_slot * width * 2, b.staged, b.count * width * 2, s.handle)` can write past the cache buffer; `poolGroups` likewise computes `rope_base = arena + (@as(u64, first_group) * width + nope) * 2` with no bounds check on `first_group + count`.
- Refactor: introduce a typed `KeyCache`/`GroupWindow` (`struct { first_slot: usize, count: usize, capacity: usize }`) with a `validate()` returning `error.BadHy4IndexRows`, and pass it to `cacheKeys`/`poolGroups` instead of raw `first_slot`/`count`.

4) `zig/src/families/qwen3_5/cuda_dspine_weights.zig` — defines `Bridge` (`alloc`, `deinit`), `total`, and the start of `version` (truncated mid-body).
- Risk: `Bridge.alloc` does `at + bytes > b.arena.len` and `b.arena.ptr + at` with unchecked `usize` arithmetic (overflow panic in safe builds), and `total` sums `L * dw.packedBytes(...)` with unchecked multiplication; `version` is cut off, so its error handling is unverifiable.
- Refactor: make `alloc` return a typed `DeviceSlice` (`struct { ptr: u64, len: usize }`) and use `std.math.add`/`mul` in `total`, returning `!usize`.

Evidence offered:
- Nemotron: checkpoint vs full precision is close (KL 0.0036–0.0137 nats on three teacher-forced prompts; 0.0077 nats over all 768 tokens; 98.4% same top token; NLL 0.0692→0.0749), and checkpoint is much faster on cold 8,192-token prompts (4.41 s vs 7.96 s, ~1.81x) with similar decode. Drafted replies equal `"draft": false` (greedy, seeded sampled, thinking), 2 and 4 concurrent streams equal solo runs, three-turn chats with regenerate/edit/delete equal a cache-off server, TP=1 and TP=2 give the same tokens on eight release prompts, prompt kernels/combine match the decode path byte-for-byte, router logits match the untiled router/host reference, and two-GB10 ranks hash/exchange every shard before serving. Speed table: one GB10 checkpoint 38.2 tok/s drafted / 18.8 draft:false / 4.41 s cold prompt; two GB10s 46.8 / 20.2; full 38.7 / 19.4 / 7.96 and 48.1 / 21.4; four concurrent greedy streams on two GB10s 6.2 s together vs 11.8 s solo; one four-image request answered first token in 11.45 s with drafted reply equal to draft:false.
- DeepSeek: token-map generator validates release geometry and records tokenizer/config SHA256; `aot-needs` executes the family’s actual symbolic planner on CPU and never opens a CUDA driver; external Triton reference tools compile every specialization for the actual target SM and write `aot/`; RoPE rows must cover context plus 2048; reference revision/compiler versions/options/manifests/hashes are kept; do not substitute captured images from another checkpoint/profile; installable ARM64 binaries are built on the native ARM64 host with real runtime and family CUDA images; compile-only targets use inert synthetic images and cannot produce a serving qualification receipt.
- MiniMax/FastH3: `tf-h3-dit` reads the checkpoint shards and a case file, runs every denoising forward, prints first-forward velocities against reference velocities, and writes final video/audio rows and first-forward velocities as raw float32; it refuses to load without M5 tensor units; arithmetic keeps bf16 weights/activations with fp32 sums and bf16 rounding where the reference rounds; attention is FastH3’s video sparse attention over 64-row tiles (text/keyframe/audio attend every tile; video attends prefix tiles plus top 20% of video tiles by pooled score; pooled branch gated in; tile means/scores/top-k/pooled branch fp32; routed attention bf16 q/k/v with fp32 scores and online softmax, weights rounded to bf16 before the value product); thirteen kernels are registered against their formulas; `dense` is kernel-work only and is not how the checkpoint was trained.
